svg.title: The Big Five subsystems of second-order arithmetic in increasing strength, from RCA-zero at the bottom to Pi-1-1 comprehension at the top, each with what it is and representative theorems

g.text: increasing strength
Π¹₁-CA₀
strongest of the five
Comprehension for Π¹₁ formulas: impredicative, quantifying over sets to build a set.
Equivalent to: the Cantor-Bendixson theorem; Silver's dichotomy for coanalytic
equivalence relations; decomposition theorems for countable abelian groups.
ATR₀
transfinite recursion
Iterate an arithmetically definable operator transfinitely along a countable well-ordering.
Equivalent to: comparability of countable well-orderings; the perfect set theorem;
Luzin's separation theorem for analytic sets; Ulm's theorem.
ACA₀
first-order part: PA
Comprehension for arithmetical formulas, no set quantifiers. This is the Turing jump.
Equivalent to: Bolzano-Weierstrass; sequential least upper bound for the reals;
Ascoli's theorem; every countable vector space has a basis.
WKL₀
the rung that matters
RCA₀ plus weak Koenig's lemma: every infinite subtree of 2<ω has an infinite path.
A COMPACTNESS principle. Panel 6 unpacks it, panel 7 gives its conservativity.
Same first-order part as RCA₀ (IΣ₁), and strictly weaker than ACA₀.
RCA₀
the base theory
Comprehension only for computable (Δ⁰₁) sets, plus Σ⁰₁ induction. Computable mathematics.
Proves outright: the intermediate value theorem; nested interval completeness;
the Baire category theorem for separable metric spaces. First-order part: IΣ₁.
